stem: A 2-year-old girl with cystic fibrosis, diagnosed on newborn screening, has had 3 days of cough productive of yellow sputum and a low-grade fever. This is the first time a respiratory culture has been sent for a chest illness. She has never been hospitalized for a chest infection or received antibiotics for one. A chest x-ray shows patchy bronchial wall thickening.
oneliner: 2F + cystic fibrosis + productive cough and low fever + first-ever respiratory culture + no prior admissions or antibiotics → organism?
ask: Which organism is most likely to grow from her sputum?

whyNot.B: Takes over **later**, after years of repeated infections and antibiotics; she has had **none** so far
whyNot.C: Acquired in late disease after prolonged contact with other patients and hospitals; she has had **no prior admissions**
whyNot.D: Causes allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis later in life; she has **fever and productive cough**, not wheeze or mucus plugs
whyNot.E: Causes **pharyngitis and skin infection**; it is not a usual airway pathogen in a young child with **cystic fibrosis**

why: In **young children** with cystic fibrosis, the first airway infections are with **Staphylococcus aureus** (and Haemophilus influenzae). **Pseudomonas aeruginosa** appears later, after repeated infections and antibiotic exposure.

bug.name: Staphylococcus aureus
bug.lab: Catalase positive, coagulase positive; golden colonies on blood agar with beta-hemolysis; ferments mannitol
bug.virulence: Protein A binds the Fc of IgG and blocks opsonization; coagulase; toxins (TSST-1, exfoliatin, enterotoxins); PBP2a makes MRSA methicillin-resistant
bug.spread: Nasal and skin carriage; direct contact; respiratory spread in cystic fibrosis
bug.causes: Skin abscesses, endocarditis, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, toxic shock, food poisoning, pneumonia (including in cystic fibrosis)

idea.rule: Cystic fibrosis airway flora follows age: S. aureus and H. influenzae in early childhood, Pseudomonas from adolescence, Burkholderia in late disease.
also: Pseudomonas aeruginosa: mucoid alginate biofilm dominates adolescent and adult disease
Burkholderia cepacia: late disease with rapid decline (cepacia syndrome) and multidrug resistance
Haemophilus influenzae: also common in early childhood
Aspergillus fumigatus: allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis in cystic fibrosis and asthma
